cards.title: One lap decides the whole race
cards.text: 22 cars, three rounds: 6 out after the first, 6 after the second, and ten left to fight for the grid that shapes everything the race can become.

cards.title: Verstappen takes it
cards.text: By 0.054s over Leclerc. Less time than a blink.

cards.title: Out before it got serious
cards.text: Alonso (P17), Albon (P18), Stroll (P19), Perez (P20), Bottas (P21), Hadjar (not classified).

cards.title: So close to the top ten
cards.text: Hulkenberg (P11), Bearman (P12), Ocon (P13), Sainz (P14), Bortoleto (P15), Colapinto (P16).

cards.title: 12 laps thrown in the bin
cards.text: In qualifying a deleted lap can be the difference between Q3 and going home early.

cards.title: Russell was quickest through the trap: 305 km/h
cards.text: Top speed says as much about wing level and the tow from the car ahead as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Nobody owned the whole lap
cards.text: The quickest sectors of the session were split between two drivers, so the ideal lap was never actually driven.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 3 times during the session
cards.text: A yellow in the wrong sector at the wrong moment ends somebody's lap, and sometimes their session.

cards.title: How the race starts
cards.text: P1 Verstappen · P2 Leclerc · P3 Hamilton · P4 Antonelli · P5 Norris · P6 Piastri
bullets: Russell qualified P6 and starts P19, 13 places further back
Stroll starts from the pit lane: the car was changed under parc ferme rules
Alonso and Hadjar start from the pit lane: the car was changed under parc ferme rules and took new power unit parts
The grid is not the qualifying order. A penalty moves a car back, whether for something on track or for a new engine, and everybody behind it moves up
